paper.title: Improving Regret Bounds for Combinatorial Semi-Bandits with Probabilistically Triggered Arms and Its Applications

settings.name_in_paper: CMAB-T (combinatorial multi-armed bandit with probabilistically triggered arms and semi-bandit feedback)
unmapped: Base arms jointly distributed on [0,1]^m (not necessarily independent); actions probabilistically trigger random subsets of base arms whose outcomes are observed
Expected reward r_S(mu) is a general (possibly nonlinear) function of the arm mean vector; action space may be infinite
Learner has access to an offline (alpha,beta)-approximation oracle; regret is the (alpha,beta)-approximation regret
Problem instance (action space, distribution class, triggering function, reward function) is known to the learner
settings.definition_quote: The environment consists of $m$ random variables $X_1, \ldots, X_m$ called {\em base arms} (or {\em arms}) following a joint distribution $D$ over $[0,1]^m$. ... When action $S_t$ is played on the environment outcome $X^{(t)}$, a random subset of arms $\tau_t \subseteq [m]$ are triggered, and the outcomes of $X^{(t)}_i$ for all $i\in \tau_t$ are observed as the feedback to the player.

settings.name_in_paper: FTP(p) fixed triggering probability CMAB-T instance (lower bound)
unmapped: m actions S_i, each triggers only base arm i with fixed probability p; reward p^{-1} X_i if triggered, 0 otherwise (rewards in [0,1/p])
Instance satisfies the non-TPM infinity-norm bounded smoothness with B=1 but not the TPM condition
settings.definition_quote: For each base arm $i \in [m]$, we define an action $S_i$ ... When playing action $S_i$ in round $t$, with a fixed probability $p$, arm $i$ is triggered and its outcome $X_i^{(t)}$ is observed, and the reward of playing $S_i$ is $p^{-1} X_i^{(t)}$; otherwise with probability $1-p$ no arm is triggered, no feedback is observed and the reward is $0$.

symbols.K_trig: maximum number of arms that can be triggered by an action, max_S |tilde S|
symbols.Delta_min_i: minimum positive gap among actions that trigger arm i with positive probability
symbols.Delta_max: maximum gap over actions triggering some arm

conditions: 1-norm TPM bounded smoothness with constant B (Condition 2)
arm outcome does not depend on whether it is triggered

source.label: thm:1-normTPM
source.quote: For the CUCB algorithm on a CMAB-T problem instance that satisfies monotonicity (Condition~\ref{cond:monotone}) and 1-norm TPM bounded smoothness (Condition~\ref{cond:1-normTPM}) with bounded smoothness constant $B$, (1) if $\Delta_{\min} > 0$, we have distribution-dependent bound $Reg_{\vmu, \alpha, \beta}(T) \le \sum_{i\in[m]} \frac{576B^2K\ln T}{\Delta_{\min}^i} + \sum_{i\in[m]}\left(\left\lceil\log_2 \frac{2BK}{\Delta_{\min}^i}\right\rceil_0 + 2\right)\cdot \frac{\pi^2}{6} \cdot \Delta_{\max} +4Bm$

results.notes: Regret is the (alpha,beta)-approximation regret defined via expected rewards r_S(mu); recorded as pseudo_regret. Paper's m (base arms) and K (max triggered set size) renamed to m_base, K_trig. Applies to cascading bandits (B=1) and influence maximization (B = C~) via Lemmas 1-2. Appendix also gives a refined version with arm-dependent B_i.

symbols.K_trig: maximum number of arms that can be triggered by an action

conditions: 1-norm TPM bounded smoothness with constant B (Condition 2)

source.label: thm:1-normTPM
source.quote: (2) we have distribution-independent bound $Reg_{\vmu, \alpha, \beta}(T) \le 12B\sqrt{mKT\ln T} + \left(\left\lceil\log_2 \frac{T}{18\ln T}\right\rceil_0+2\right) \cdot m \cdot \frac{\pi^2}{6}\cdot \Delta_{\max} +2Bm.$

results.notes: Distribution-independent bound (still contains Delta_max in lower-order term).

symbols.m_base: number of base arms (= number of actions) m

source.label: thm:indlowerbound
source.quote: Let $p$ be a real number with $0< p < 1$. Then for any CMAB-T algorithm $A$, if $T \ge 6p^{-1}$, there exists a CMAB-T environment instance $D$ with mean $\vmu$ such that on instance FTP($p$), $Reg_{\vmu}^A(T) \ge \frac{1}{170}\sqrt{\frac{m T}{p}}.$

results.notes: Shows 1/p^* factor is unavoidable without the TPM condition.

source.label: thm:deplowerbound
source.quote: For any consistent algorithm $A$ running on instance FTP($p$) and $\mu_i < 1$ for every arm $i$, we have $$\liminf_{T\to +\infty} \frac{Reg^A_{\vmu}(T)}{\ln T} \ge \sum_{i:\mu_i<\mu^*} \frac{p^{-1}\Delta_i}{\kl(\mu_i, \mu^*)},$$

results.notes: Consistent: every non-optimal arm played o(T^a) times for all a>0.

symbols.K_trig: maximum action size (arms triggered by an action)
symbols.Delta_min_i: minimum positive gap of actions containing arm i

source.label: thm:1-norm.nontriggering
source.quote: For the CUCB algorithm on a CMAB (without triggering, i.e. $p^*=1$) problem that satisfies 1-norm bounded smoothness (Condition~\ref{cond:1-norm}) with bounded smoothness constant $B$, 1. if $\Delta_{\min} > 0$, we have distribution-dependent bound $Reg_{\vmu, \alpha, \beta}(T) \le \sum_{i\in[m]}\frac{48B^2K\ln T}{\Delta_{\min}^i} + 2Bm + \frac{\pi^2}{3}\cdot m\cdot \Delta_{\max};$

results.notes: Generalizes linear combinatorial semi-bandits (Kveton et al. 2015). Monotonicity not stated in theorem but used implicitly in proof.

source.label: thm:1-norm.nontriggering
source.quote: 2. we have distribution-independent bound $Reg_{\vmu, \alpha, \beta}(T) \le 14B\sqrt{KmT\ln T} + 2Bm + \frac{\pi^2}{3}\cdot m\cdot \Delta_{\max};$

symbols.G_i: Delta_min^i/f^{-1}(Delta_min^i)^2 + integral from Delta_min^i to Delta_max^i of 1/f^{-1}(x)^2 dx
symbols.finv_Delta_min: f^{-1}(Delta_min), inverse bounded smoothness function at the minimum gap

conditions: infinity-norm TPM bounded smoothness with function f (Condition 6)

source.label: thm:inf-norm
source.quote: For the CUCB algorithm on a problem instance that satisfies TPM bounded smoothness (Condition~\ref{cond:globalTPM}) with bounded smoothness function $f(x)$, together with $\Delta_{\min}>0$, the regret is at most \sum_{i\in [m]} 78\ln T \left(\frac{\Delta_{\min}^i}{f^{-1}(\Delta_{\min}^i)^2} + \int_{\Delta_{\min}^i}^{\Delta_{\max}^i}\frac{1}{f^{-1}(x)^2}\dx\right) + m \cdot [...] \cdot \Delta_{\max};

symbols.a_sm: slope of linear bounded smoothness function f(x)=a x

conditions: infinity-norm TPM bounded smoothness with f(x)=a x (Condition 6)

source.label: thm:inf-norm
source.quote: For the CUCB algorithm on a problem instance that satisfies TPM bounded smoothness (Condition~\ref{cond:globalTPM}) with bounded smoothness function $f(x)=ax$, the regret is at most $$25a\sqrt{mT\ln T} + m \cdot \left[\left(\frac{\pi^2}{6}+1\right) \left\lceil-\log_2 (\sqrt{156m\ln T/T})\right\rceil_0 + \frac{\pi^2}{3}+1\right] \cdot \Delta_{\max};$$

symbols.B_i: relative 1-norm TPM bounded smoothness constant of arm i
symbols.K_trig: maximum number of arms triggered by an action
symbols.Delta_min_i: minimum positive gap among actions triggering arm i

conditions: relative 1-norm TPM bounded smoothness with vector B and reference optimal action mapping (Condition 7)

source.label: thm:relative.1-normTPM
source.quote: For the CUCB algorithm on a CMAB-T problem instance that satisfies monotonicity (Condition~\ref{cond:monotone}), and a distribution and a reference optimal action mapping $\ro(\cdot)$ that satisfy the relative 1-norm TPM bounded smoothness (Condition~\ref{cond:relative.1-normTPM}) with $\vB$, (1) if $\Delta_{\min} > 0$, we have gap-dependent bound ...

results.notes: For linear rewards with 0-1 action vectors, B_i = 0 for arms in the optimal action, so the sum runs over non-optimal arms only.

symbols.B_i: relative 1-norm TPM bounded smoothness constant of arm i

source.label: thm:relative.1-normTPM
source.quote: (2) we have \emph{gap}-independent bound (it is not distribution-independent, because it depends on $\ro(\cdot)$) $Reg_{\vmu, \alpha, \beta}(T) \le 12\sqrt{\sum_{i\in[m]}B_i^2mT\ln T} + \left(\left\lceil\log_2 \frac{T}{18\ln T}\right\rceil_0+2\right) \cdot m \cdot \frac{\pi^2}{6}\cdot \Delta_{\max} +\sum_{i\in[m]}2B_i.$

results.notes: Statement uses m inside the sqrt (vs K in Appendix refinement); recorded as printed. Gap-independent but instance-dependent through B_i (depends on reference optimal action).
